steps.title: Everyone the club talks to lives here
steps.body: Sponsors, alumni, faculty, schools. Open the Contacts tab.

steps.title: Set a follow-up before you save
steps.body: A date, not "sometime." This field is the whole reason a contact record is worth keeping — pick a day you'd actually chase them.

steps.title: Make someone up, then save
steps.body: This is your training space — name, org, email. Nobody will ever be emailed from this tour.

steps.title: Open a contact
steps.body: Every contact is a card on this board, and the column it sits in is how warm they are. Click this one to open it.

steps.title: Switch to Timeline
steps.body: Info is who they are. Timeline is what has actually happened. Open it.

steps.title: Interaction history
steps.body: Who spoke to them, when, and what was promised. That last one is what gets forgotten, and it's the reason a sponsor stops replying. Log one now if you like.

steps.title: Campaigns group contacts you're working through together
steps.body: Close the drawer and open the Campaigns tab.

steps.title: Name it after the ask, not the season
steps.body: "Titanium sponsors for Rascal" tells the next officer what it was for. "Fall outreach" doesn't. Fill it in and save.

steps.title: Coverage at a glance
steps.body: Contacted, replied, untouched. That middle column is the one that matters — a campaign where everyone was contacted and nobody replied is telling you something about the message, not the list.

steps.title: Overdue follow-ups DM you
steps.body: Every weekday morning. You won't have to remember to come back here — which is the only reason setting a real date on that contact was worth doing.
